stories.completed: Done. You reached the final study summary screen.

items.title: Create medical flashcards
items.description: Create a deck, add two basic cards and study them through to the summary.
steps: Tap “Add deck” and create a new set.
Add the first basic card and tap “Next”.
Add the second card and tap “Save” to return to the deck.
Tap “Study” in the top-right corner of the deck.
Go through the cards until the summary screen.

items.title: Turn pharmacology notes into cloze cards
items.description: Create a deck, add one cloze card and finish a short study session.
steps: Tap “Add deck” and create a new set.
Select part of the text, use cloze and tap “Save”.
Tap “Study” in the top-right corner of the deck.
Go through study until the summary screen.

items.title: Review before a colloquium
items.description: Start studying from an example deck and reach the repeat-or-exit choice.
steps: Tap “Study” on one of the example decks.
Rate each card as “I know” or “I don't know”.
On the final screen, choose repeat or return to the deck.

fixedScreens.label: Decks
fixedScreens.title: Three subjects, zero study clutter
fixedScreens.description: Anatomy, pharmacology and pathology stay organized in focused decks. Tags make it easy to find exactly what belongs to a topic or exam.

fixedScreens.label: Flashcards
fixedScreens.title: Use the right format for every fact
fixedScreens.description: Mix classic questions, cloze deletions, images and image occlusion in the same deck. Everything stays organized and ready to study.

fixedScreens.label: Cloze deletion
fixedScreens.title: Turn notes into active recall
fixedScreens.description: Select a key phrase and Fishki turns it into a cloze while keeping the answer on the back. No need to rewrite the same fact twice.

fixedScreens.label: Smart reviews
fixedScreens.title: Review at the right moment
fixedScreens.description: Fishki builds your queue with FSRS. Rate each answer with a simple gesture, and the app schedules the next review for the right time.

fixedScreens.label: Images
fixedScreens.title: Study from diagrams that explain the mechanism
fixedScreens.description: Add an image to either side of a card. Fishki keeps the full graphic visible, so important structures and labels are never cropped away.

fixedScreens.label: Image occlusion
fixedScreens.title: Test structures without revealing the answer
fixedScreens.description: Cover a node, vessel or part of a specimen and identify it from memory. Flip the card to reveal the complete image and the marked location.

fixedScreens.label: Daily plan
fixedScreens.title: Open Fishki and know what to study today
fixedScreens.description: FSRS and the exam planner combine new cards, due reviews and difficult material into one realistic daily plan.

steps.title: Choose editing or start studying
steps.description: Every deck has a separate action for managing cards and starting a study session quickly.

steps.title: See its cards and add another
steps.description: Opening a deck shows its flashcards. The floating button opens the new-card editor directly.

steps.title: Enter the question and answer
steps.description: The editor stays simple while supporting formatting, images and serious medical content.

steps.title: Choose how you want to study
steps.description: Choose free-form quick study or smart reviews scheduled by FSRS. Both modes share the same progress.

steps.title: Move through material without extra ratings
steps.description: Flip the card and choose only “I know” or “I don't know”.

steps.title: See your session result
steps.description: Check mastery and repeat only the cards you missed when needed.

useCases.intro: Fishki gives images, diagrams, classifications and structured answers the space they need without making card creation complicated.

proof.heading: Built around how medical students actually study
proof.footer: Medical students told us the same things repeatedly: creating cards takes too long, images are awkward to use, review systems feel cumbersome and offline study is unreliable. Fishki tackles those problems directly.

quotes.name: Hannah
quotes.quote: I want reviews like in Anki, but with simpler syncing between my phone, computer and offline mode.

quotes.name: Kate
quotes.quote: The best option would combine Anki and Quizlet: quick review and regular spaced repetition.

quotes.name: Adam
quotes.quote: I would like more control: changing intervals, shuffling flashcards and easily swapping the question and answer.
